sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023 before jumping 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025 [D130][D284][D338][D393].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217%, driven by Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was again data center compute and networking, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [D448][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Compute was 75.2% of revenue and added 46.1pp, while Networking added 14.1pp [D627][D629][D636].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, so incremental operating margin was 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% against net income growth of 64.7%, with the diluted share count down 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026, against a window median of 32.8%, a high of 62.4% in FY2025 and a low of 15.7% in FY2023 [F50][D813][D812][D811].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the main drag on the 2.0pp operating-margin decline [F30][D462][D463].
Compute & Networking operating income absorbed a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase-obligation charge in the first quarter of FY2026 [P7].
R&D rose 43.2% on a 29% increase in compensation and a 79% increase in compute and infrastructure, though it still added 1.3pp to margin [D466][P5][D478].
Net margin trailed operating margin by 4.8pp as other income of $11.1 billion, largely unrealized equity gains including Intel, lifted pre-tax income [D861][X120][P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, the window low against a median of 0.97x [F100][F60][D435][D851].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, just under the 46.6% FY2025 high [F110][D432][D821].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x in FY2025 [F105][D431][D437][D382].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, pushing days inventory to 125 and days sales outstanding to 65 [D474][D473][D446][D445].
Total debt was $8.47 billion against $10.6 billion of cash, and short-term investments were not reported in FY2026, so net cash is understated [D440][F150][R3].
Return on average equity was 101.5%, in the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a 20.3% median [D447][D848][D849].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends of $974 million were 42.5% of free cash flow [X150][X160][D444].
Acquisitions of $1.54 billion and higher equity purchases drove investing outflow of $52.2 billion [X168][F120][P1].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 after $34.6 billion in FY2025, so net cash and its peer rank omit them [R3][X188].
Two direct customers were 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, both mainly in Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026 and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2% [D545][D544][D541].
The Graphics segment was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023, a past cyclicality marker [D753][D754][R1].
If gross margin falls below the FY2026 level of 71.1%, the H20 charge would look structural rather than one-off [F30].
If operating cash flow to net income stays below the 0.86x FY2026 level, working-capital build is outpacing earnings [D435].
If Data Center share drops below 89.7%, the concentration that drove the window would be diluting [D620].
